name: Dumbbell Incline Bench Press
movementPattern: Incline chest press - free weight dumbbell
grip: Pronated or semi-pronated grip holding dumbbells at shoulder level with wrists stacked over forearms.
description: Press two dumbbells upward from upper-chest level while lying on an incline bench angled between 30 and 45 degrees, allowing an unrestricted pressing path and deep stretch for upper pectoral development.
setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline between 30 and 45 degrees.
Sit with a dumbbell resting upright on each knee, back pressed firmly against the pad, feet flat on the floor.
Kick the dumbbells up to your shoulders with your knees one at a time as you lie back on the incline pad.
Position the dumbbells beside your upper chest with forearms vertical and elbows tucked at approximately 45 degrees to your torso.
instructions: Press both dumbbells upward and slightly inward in a smooth, converging vertical path.
Extend your arms fully overhead without violently locking your elbows or banging the dumbbells together.
Pause briefly at peak contraction over your upper chest.
Lower the dumbbells slowly under complete control back to the deep chest stretch position beside your upper pectorals before beginning the next repetition.
cues: Press up and converge over the upper chest.
Control the lowering into a deep chest stretch.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows out to 90 degrees, causing anterior shoulder impingement.
Setting the incline too steep (>45 degrees), shifting load from the chest to the anterior deltoids.
Banging the dumbbells together at the top of the press.

logging.example: Two 26 kg dumbbells: record 26 kg per dumbbell.
logging.note: Record the mass of an individual dumbbell rather than the combined total pair mass.

variantNote: Incline dumbbell chest press with independent arm movement. Allows greater range of motion and personalized wrist rotation compared to fixed barbell pressing.
